title: Schema fidelity robustness: timer-based interruption & toolcall compatibility smoke
creator: Anika Shah
description: Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable smoke harness that validates schema fidelity under timing-related stress and mid-stream toolcall interruptions. This ticket covers building the harness, instrumenting telemetry for deterministic detection of schema violations, and a 3-stage runbook for failures (recover, degrade, alert). The harness must run against multiple model variants and runtime kernel settings and produce machine-readable results for CI ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: A smoke harness that runs within CI (<= 10m) and exercises: streaming partial outputs, forced tool/function call interleavings, and artificial network pauses/packets delays.

Detected schema violations are classified into categories: complete-parse-fail, field-mismatch, type-coercion, missing-toolcall-sentinel, and truncated-json. Each run emits a summary JSON with counts for each category.
Telemetry hooks emit traces and token-level annotations to the observability pipeline (trace id included in summary).
False-positive rate on a golden set is <= 1% across three model variants (open-1.3b, open-7b, redwood-tuned-13b), with documented known failure modes.
Automated PR checks fail on any new regression compared to baseline for the dominant model used by the PR (comparison mode configurable).
tasks: Design harness API and CLI: args for model, runtime profile, delay schedule, and toolcall script
Implement streaming input driver that can inject pauses and simulated network jitter
Implement a toolcall simulator that can preempt the stream at token boundaries and optionally drop a tool response
Schema validator that tolerates order-insensitive object fields but flags missing required keys
Integrate lightweight telemetry markers: trace-id, request-id, token-range for violations
Create CI job and baseline dataset (golden prompts + expected schema traces)
Run baseline across 3 model variants and capture baseline artifacts
Document runbook + remediation guidance for each violation category
test_plan:
1) Baseline run: execute harness against golden prompts using no injected delays to collect baseline success metrics.
2) Timer sweep: introduce deterministic delay patterns (fixed pause, exponential jitter, packet-drop) and validate schema outcomes across sweep values.
3) Toolcall interruption: replay scenarios where a toolcall is initiated mid-stream, tool response is delayed, or tool response contains malformed JSON; assert that the decoder either recovers to a known fallback or fails with an appropriate classification.
4) Parameter matrix: for temperature in [0.0,0.2,0.8], top_p in [0.7,0.95], and streaming-chunk-size [16,64,256], run cross product against models and collect failure histograms.
5) CI gating: add a fast smoke (subset) that runs on PRs and a nightly full run that populates dashboards.
6) Manual review: triage any new failure types and add to known-failures map or convert to a bug with reproduction steps.
notes: Trade-offs: strict order enforcement would reduce false-positives but break legitimate order-insensitive schemas; this harness uses configurable sensitivity per-schema.
We intentionally keep harness runtime short for PR feedback; full exhaustive runs live in nightly jobs.
We will reuse existing streaming test infra where possible but extend it with token-level annotations for schema checks.
